## Natural-language hypothesis (grounded in BH-adjusted p-values)

Across every studied domain — Cognitive, Social, and Economics — effect-size estimates are systematically larger in original studies than in their paired replications (signed comparison on the Fisher-z scale). All three disciplines reject the null of no difference after Benjamini–Hochberg correction across the three discipline tests (α = 0.05): Cognitive (median ΔFisher-z = +0.249, p_BH = 4.85 × 10⁻⁶, n = 34), Social (median ΔFisher-z = +0.232, p_BH = 1.73 × 10⁻⁶, n = 34), and Economics (median ΔFisher-z = +0.143, p_BH = 4.20 × 10⁻⁴, n = 18). The asymmetry is largest in absolute terms in Cognitive Psychology and Social Psychology, and remains decisive — same signed direction — in Experimental Economics even after retaining the 18 sign-flipped replications and applying FDR control.

payload.hypothesis: Across every studied domain — Cognitive, Social, and Economics — effect-size estimates are systematically larger in original studies than in their paired replications (signed comparison on the Fisher-z scale). All three disciplines reject the null of no difference after Benjamini-Hochberg correction across the three discipline tests (alpha=0.05): Cognitive (median DeltaFisher-z = +0.249, p_BH = 4.85e-06, n=34), Social (median DeltaFisher-z = +0.232, p_BH = 1.73e-06, n=34), and Economics (median DeltaFisher-z = +0.143, p_BH = 4.20e-04, n=18). payload.workflow: Loaded /workspace/data/meta-regression_joined_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (86 rows, 60 cols). Computed signed paired difference d = fiso - fisr per row. Grouped by discipline (Cognitive n=34, Social n=34, Economics n=18) and as sensitivity by project.x (Psychology n=68, Experimental Economics n=18). For each group ran: one-sided paired Wilcoxon signed-rank (alternative='greater'), one-sided one-sample t on d (alternative='greater'), 95% Student-t CI on mean(d), bootstrap BCa 95% CI on median(d) with 10,000 seed-fixed resamples and jackknife acceleration. Applied Benjamini-Hochberg FDR and Holm-Bonferroni across the 3 discipline tests. relative_es treated descriptively only; the 18 sign-flipped Economics replications retained throughout. Implemented and executed by /workspace/artifacts/analysis/analysis.py.
